title: Grateful Dead Live at The Spectrum on 1973-09-21
lineage: Akai GX636 direct tape head output  > Bottlehead tube tape pre w/a pair of Telefunken tubes circa 1960  > Apogee Mini Me 24/96  > Apogee Mini DAC monitoring and mastering  > FLAC
source: most likely MR > R @3 & 3/4 ips - dub of Jerry's reel left at a girlfriends house done by Will Boswell was done back in the Spring of '79

ai_review.summary: Soundboard recording with some harsh cuts but captures a strong second‑set jam featuring He's Gone > Truckin' > The Other One and horn‑enhanced numbers.
ai_review.review: The show is praised for its energetic second set, the early placement of The Other One, and the added horns that lift tracks like Wharf Rat and Casey Jones. Recording quality is decent for a 1973 board tape but suffers from noticeable cuts in songs such as Sugaree, Big River and Playin' In The Band, plus occasional firecracker noise, making parts of the performance unevenly presented.

ai_rating.rationale: Show quality is high (strong jams, good set flow) while recording quality is marred by harsh cuts and missing sections; the weighted average yields a solid but not stellar rating.

recording_quality.technical_notes: Board tape with harsh cuts in Sugaree, Big River, Playin' In The Band and missing portions of The Other One; occasional firecracker noise; overall decent clarity when present.

show_quality.setlist_flow: First set ends with a driving Playing In The Band; second set is a continuous jam through He's Gone > Truckin' > The Other One > Wharf Rat > Row Jimmy, followed by a horn‑filled encore that adds extra excitement.

band_member_comments.Jerry: Garcia's guitar tone and improvisational choices are highlighted as superb; his use of early MIDI ideas is noted in the horn sections.
band_member_comments.Phil: Phil's bass line on The Other One is described as surprising and powerful, though a few vocal mix issues are mentioned.
band_member_comments.Bob: Weir receives praise for strong vocals on 'Row Jimmy' and overall contribution to the set’s energy.
band_member_comments.Keys: Keith's vocal levels are said to be off in places but his keyboard work helps fill out the sound; horns complement his playing.
